historical_sources.excerpt:
The NFT identifier is derived from the canonical chain ID, vault address and a monotonic mint sequence. `mintDormant()` creates the canonical vault record and NFT before any LP is supplied. Activation and later LP replacements preserve that identifier. The canonical-chain guard prevents satellite issuance. A satellite vault holds the same economic identifier but never mints another ZZZ NFT for it.

A dormant economic NFT has no Uniswap LP NFT. An active economic NFT has one active Uniswap LP NFT. This preserves direct fee attribution for supported pools but is not gas-optimal for a large collection. An aggregated-share vault would be a different accounting design, not a drop-in optimization.

record.title: Transaction costs must bind the original signed fee review

historical_sources.label: SV-01
historical_sources.heading: Addressed findings
historical_sources.excerpt: | SV-01 | Medium | Keeper receipt accounting trusted the derived `effectiveGasPrice` and did not bind signed gas/cap/chain fields to the original fee review. An inconsistent RPC receipt could understate/overstate spent gas, corrupting future daily-budget decisions or unnecessarily stopping maintenance. The keeper now captures the bounded fee review durably before invoking the signer, validates transaction chain, exact gas limit and fee cap, and derives type-2 execution price from signed caps and the canonical inclusion block's base fee. Types 0/1 require agreement with signed `gasPrice`; unknown transaction fee types are rejected. |

historical_sources.label: SV-02
historical_sources.heading: Addressed findings
historical_sources.excerpt: | SV-02 | Medium | Actual separate L1 fees could exceed the allowance used during submission review without a failed reconciliation. The original fee semantics and L1/total maximum now remain attached to the pending intent. Missing required separate L1 evidence or a captured-bound violation preserves pending state and stops reconciliation. A later configuration cannot reinterpret an earlier pending transaction. |

historical_sources.label: K04

record.title: Foreign/reset acknowledgement and interrupted evidence recovery

historical_sources.label: Persistent faults could cause repeated paid clear transactions
historical_sources.heading: Material changes
historical_sources.excerpt: | Persistent faults could cause repeated paid clear transactions. | Canonical reset acknowledgement suppresses duplicate clears while waiting for healthy reads; fresh nonempty foreign evidence forces a new reset and observe intent invalidates the acknowledgement atomically. | No cached readiness, receipt bypass or automatic budget increase. |
historical_sources.group_label: Persistent faults could cause repeated paid clear transactions

historical_sources.label: Foreign evidence after an acknowledged clear
historical_sources.heading: Findings and repairs
historical_sources.excerpt: | Foreign evidence after an acknowledged clear | After a healthy empty read, the old keeper dropped its clear acknowledgement when another record appeared, adopting observations it had not maintained. Any nonempty record while the acknowledgement remains now requires another reset; only the keeper's own atomic observe intent removes that acknowledgement. This closes a service-level evidence gap; the contract still enforces sampled readiness. | [Keeper](../../keeper/monitor.py), [regressions](../../tests_python/test_keeper_confirmation_followup.py) |
historical_sources.group_label: Foreign evidence after an acknowledged clear / Initial raw-read failures bypassed reset handling

historical_sources.label: Initial raw-read failures bypassed reset handling
historical_sources.heading: Findings and repairs
historical_sources.excerpt: | Initial raw-read failures bypassed reset handling | Unreadable/malformed Vault group or pool/accounting input, or an initial global Access/clock failure, could leave an old window and jitter reusable after recovery. Relevant bucket faults now invalidate that bucket; initial global faults invalidate known fresh windows. Pending recovery runs first and never acquires these new dependencies. Unrelated share/job failures remain separate. | [Keeper](../../keeper/monitor.py), [failure-isolation cases](../../tests_python/test_keeper_confirmation_followup.py) |
historical_sources.group_label: Foreign evidence after an acknowledged clear / Initial raw-read failures bypassed reset handling

historical_sources.label: Confirmation coordination
historical_sources.heading: Delivered changes
historical_sources.excerpt: | Confirmation coordination | A live worker's proved inside/opposite-side observation cannot preserve a known nonempty ordinary outside window. Same-hash helper evidence feeds existing durable reset/ack scheduling; foreign nonempty evidence after a clear is forced once. Empty/manual/cleared evidence must not cause repeated paid resets. Pure physical readers and the diagnostic command never mutate this state. Missing configuration is separate from an interrupted raw physical read. No new timer or namespace. |

original.actual_heading: ### Core-C2: the buyback maximum used the lower input USD mark
original.excerpt:
`ZZZBuyback.execute` previously compared `Oracle.value` with `operatingTradeUSD`. `Oracle.value` deliberately returns the lower of the two admitted USD bounds. With accepted prices of $1.00 and $1.03, a $20 lower-mark trade could pass a $20 ceiling while its upper-mark input value was $20.60. This understated the configured maximum spend; it did not by itself bypass the separate conservative swap minimum or redirect holder rewards.

The maximum now uses the upper input price, rounded upward in USD18 units. A zero ceiling still stops before source/reserve calls. Missing, stale or invalid dual-source output does not fall back to the historical lower-only interface. Oracle display/minimum semantics, the existing upper-input/lower-output swap quote, actual reserve release, burn verification, allocations and permissions are unchanged. Acceptance is narrower so the reviewed per-trade ceiling holds at either admitted input price. This is a per-trade ceiling, not a new cumulative budget.

Sources: [Buyback](../../src/ZZZBuyback.sol), [Oracle semantics](../../src/ZZZOracle.sol), [operating and boundary checks](../../test/BuybackOperatingLimit.t.sol), [composed execution checks](../../test/BuybackExecution.t.sol).
